title: Data retention and training use by plan

opening.headline: Even if the model is the same, the conditions for storing and using the entered data are different for personal accounts and company accounts.
body: The same meeting materials can be pasted into a personal account chat window or into a company account. Although the two accounts appear to have the same model, they differ in how much data is kept and how much data can be used to improve the model. If you don't know the difference, material you thought was safe could last longer than expected.

In this class, you'll see Anthropic's consumer and commercial documents side-by-side and learn about three comparison criteria: retention period, learning availability, and administrator control. Next, we compare the conditions of OpenAI API and Google Workspace in the same framework, and use examples to see what changes occur when the same data is entered into a personal account and a corporate account.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Explain the differences in retention and learning usage between consumer and enterprise plans
Distinguish how plan differences impact data exposure

screens.title: Personal account and company account, where should I put it safely?
screens.lead: Let's look at a scene where the same data is put into two accounts. Read below and think about what might be different.

visual.alt: An illustration of the same document icon being split into a personal account box and a company account box.
labels: How long will it be stored?
Will it be used for learning?

paragraphs: The same meeting materials can be pasted into the chat window of a personal account or a company account. The screens are similar and the models look the same. However, different data processing terms apply to the two accounts.

If you are not aware that conditions are different, materials you put in believing they are safe may remain longer than expected or be used for unintended purposes. Conversely, if you know the conditions, you can decide based on the sensitivity of the data which account to put it in.
The goal of this class is to create a framework for comparing the retention and learning usage terms of consumer and business plans.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: If two accounts use the same model, what is the same and what is different? Answer this question at the end of class.

screens.outro: Now that I know there is a difference, let me first recall what I know.

screens.title: Do you know the difference between my work account and my personal account?
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to enter or submit your answer, so think about it in your head first and then press it.

items.answer: This is the retention period. Retention periods vary depending on the plan and service, as well as when the user deletes the conversation and when the provider must retain it. This is the first comparison standard for this class.

items.prompt: Are the conversations used to improve the model?
items.answer: This is whether you use learning or not. For consumer use, the user may decide whether or not to allow it through settings, and for business use or API, it is often notified that it will not be used for learning without consent. This is the second comparison standard.

This is administrator control. In an organizational account, the owner or administrator can set features, apps, and retention periods, and individuals can only use them within those limits. This is the third comparison standard.

screens.outro: Now that we've organized the questions into three categories, let's look at Anthropic's personal and organizational documents side by side.

screens.title: View Anthropic personal and organizational preservation documents side by side
screens.lead: Switch between the two states to compare retention, deletion, training usage, and exceptions for consumer and organizational documents for the same company.

visual.alt: Comparison diagram showing the core of consumer and commercial documents divided into left and right sides.

states.label: For personal use (consumer use)
states.body: Consumer documents such as Claude Free, Pro, and Max. When you delete a conversation, it immediately disappears from your conversation history and is deleted from backend storage within 30 days. If you allow your data to be used to improve the model, it can be kept in de-identified form during training for up to 5 years, and you can change this setting at any time. If you turn the setting off, neither old nor new conversations will be used for future model training. As an exception, if an automated system flags a suspected violation of our usage policy, inputs and outputs may be stored for up to 2 years, and may be retained for longer if required by law.

states.label: For organizational use (commercial use)
states.body: Documentation for commercial products such as Claude for Work and API. The API principle is to automatically delete input and output from the backend within 30 days after receiving them. However, there are exceptions when using a longer retention service controlled by the user, when there is a separate agreement such as zero data retention, when longer retention is required to enforce the usage policy, or when it is necessary to comply with the law. Products that can save and continue conversations keep conversations within the product for a consistent experience and allow users to delete them from the dashboard. The Anthropic API documentation states that preserved data will not be used to train models without explicit permission.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen the differences between personal and organizational use within a company, let's expand on APIs and terms for other companies.

screens.title: API and Workspace Retention Terms: OpenAI and Google
screens.lead: The table below shows how retention periods, whether learning is enabled, and who controls each service vary. Compare by reading the same horizontal lines.

data.notes: Google says generative AI does not change its existing privacy commitments, and that it processes customer data only as directed in its data processing agreements.

screens.outro: Now that we've compared the terms, let's take a look at what an organization's managers can decide on.

screens.title: Administrator Controls: What the Organization Decides
screens.lead: Hover over or select an underlined term in the description below to see a short description. Check the items that the administrator can set one by one.

data.text: In organizational accounts, administrators can modify usage conditions. In ChatGPT Enterprise workspaces, owners and administrators set member access, feature access, apps, analytics, and identity management. Once an organization's unique AI policy information window is defined, it is displayed to users every 30 days and whenever the content changes. Google administrators have default settings enabled for services such as Gmail, Drive, and Docs (You can turn Gemini features on and off for each service.). Gemini Notebook settings are also controlled by administrators. In this way, even with the same model, Organization settings allows users to customize the conditions they use.

terms.tip: In ChatGPT Enterprise, if owners and administrators set organization-specific AI policy guidance, this is a window that is displayed to users every 30 days and when the content changes.

terms.term: You can turn Gemini features on and off for each service.
terms.tip: Google administrators can turn Gemini features on or off for each Workspace service, such as Gmail, Calendar, or Drive. You can also apply it only to organizational units or groups.
It is a research aid tool that uploads data and obtains answers based on that data. Administrators can turn it on and off for each user.
Settings such as features, apps, and retention periods are determined on a workspace basis by the owner or administrator. Users of personal accounts are not protected or controlled by this setting.

screens.outro: Now that we've looked at all three criteria, let's solve an example of inserting the same data into two accounts.

screens.title: Explanation: When putting the same data into a personal account and when putting it into a corporate account
screens.lead: A step-by-step comparison is made when the instructor places a draft client proposal into two accounts. Select the right arrow to proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Check the data
steps.body: The material is a draft proposal before sending it to the business partner. Since this is internal data that has not yet been made public, how it remains external is important. We compare putting this data into a personal account versus putting it into a corporate account based on the same three criteria.

steps.title: Step 1 Preservation and Learning of Personal Accounts
steps.body: Personal accounts are subject to consumer terms. When you clear a conversation, it immediately disappears from your history and is deleted from the backend within 30 days. However, if the Allow model enhancements setting is turned on, they may be kept in de-identified form for up to 5 years.

steps.title: Step 2: Control of personal accounts
steps.body: Personal accounts are outside the protection of company retention and deletion policies or administrator settings. Your organization cannot see or control this usage. Although the data was within the company, the processing conditions would depend on the settings chosen by the individual.

steps.title: Tier 3 corporate account
steps.body: Enterprise accounts have commercial terms and retention periods and features determined by your organization's settings. Administrators control features and apps, and the organization determines the scope of what users can use.

steps.title: Step 4 Comparison
steps.body: Even if the model is the same, the retention period, whether learning is used, and the control entity are different. Therefore, choosing a safe account is based on the processing conditions document, not the model name.

screens.outro: Let's summarize what you need to check to see if all corporate accounts are safe.

screens.title: Commentary: Check even if it is a corporate account
screens.lead: By selecting and expanding each item, you can see the questions you need to ask and why, even if you are using a corporate account.

items.title: Terms and conditions may vary by service.
items.body: Even for the same corporate account, retention conditions vary depending on chat, API, and workspace apps. For example, use of Anthropic's Claude Console is not within the scope of zero data retention, and product screens for Claude Teams and Enterprise are also not subject to this approach. Check the document corresponding to the service you are using.

items.title: Check 1: Retention period and change rights
items.body: Find out how long conversation records are kept, and whether that period can be changed by the administrator. Some services, like Gemini in Workspace, allow administrators to set an automatic retention period, while others allow users to set their conversation history not to be saved.

items.title: Check 2: Whether learning is enabled or not
items.body: Check how it is used for learning. API and Workspace are notified to not be used for learning without permission, but for consumer use, it is up to the user's settings. The answer varies depending on the account type, so check each account separately.

items.title: Check 3: Separate commitments such as zero data retention
items.body: Conditions that require separate agreements, such as zero data retention, are not automatically applied. Since it can only be used by approved customers and is set at the organizational level, we need to make sure it actually applies to our organization.

items.title: Check 4: Exceptions kept longer
items.body: We may retain your information longer than the default retention period due to policy violation investigations or legal requirements. Know what the exception conditions are and check this by reading the conditions document and leaving a justification.

screens.outro: Now that we've organized the checklist, let's review the key points.

screens.title: Key takeaway: Data processing conditions vary depending on the plan
screens.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class. Read the first question, remembering what is the same and what is different between personal and company accounts.

paragraphs: Even for the same model, data processing conditions vary depending on the plan. For consumer use, user settings drive retention and for enterprise use, and for enterprise use, contract and administrator settings drive retention and learning usage. The answer to the first question is that although the model is the same, the retention period, whether learning is used, and the control entity are different.

Conditions are compared based on three criteria: retention period, learning availability, and administrator control. And the basis is confirmed in the relevant provider's documents. We do not judge based on model name or screen similarity.

callout.label: standards to remember
callout.text: Before uploading materials, document the retention period, learning availability, and administrator controls for this account.

glossary.def: This is the period for which input, output, and conversation records remain in the provider's system.
This is a condition for whether the conversation can be used to improve the model.
Personal plans and organizational plans are presented in separate documents with different retention, learning, and management requirements.
Permission for organization administrators to turn features, apps, and retention settings on or off.
This is a separate agreement that prevents the provider from retaining approved customer content.

misconceptions.myth: When you delete a conversation, it immediately disappears from everywhere.
misconceptions.fact: It disappears from conversation history immediately, but is deleted from backend storage within a set period of time. Anthropic says within 30 days. It can be included in a training process that is already in progress or in a model that has already been trained.

misconceptions.myth: If it is a company account, the conditions are the same no matter which function you use.
misconceptions.fact: Retention conditions vary depending on your settings and services, such as chat, API, and workspace apps. You must check the documentation corresponding to the service you are using.

misconceptions.myth: All paid plans are not used for learning.
misconceptions.fact: Learning usage conditions are provided separately for each plan. For consumer use, it may be determined by the user's settings, so you should check with the document of the plan, not whether it is paid.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Even for the same model, data processing conditions vary depending on the plan.
Conditions are compared by retention period, whether learning is enabled, and administrator control.
Personal accounts are outside the protection of your organization's retention policies and administrator settings.
The basis for the conditions can be checked in the relevant provider's documentation.
